STEP 1 - Vessel type: shallow-to-medium stainless steel mixing bowl, curved inner wall visible on all sides, food sitting well below the rim. Deep bowl.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: a stainless mixing bowl like this is typically a medium-large prep bowl, roughly 22-26 cm across.
b) Reference cue: the bowl spans most of the frame height (about 480 px), and the food mound occupies roughly a third of the bowl's width. No fork or utensil is visible for scale, so I rely on the type cue. Taking the bowl width as about 24 cm.
Final width = 24 cm.

STEP 3 - Food items:
Capacity = 0.35 x 24^3 / 1000 = 0.35 x 13.82 = 4.84 L (deep bowl).
The food sits well below the rim: the mound surface is about 40-50% of the depth, so fill is roughly 0.4 by depth (fill^2 = 0.16 for volume).
Food volume = 4.84 L x 0.16 = 0.77 L = 775 ml.

Items split by visible share:
- Sliced white onion (about 50%): 388 ml x 0.6 = 233 g. Onion kcal ~40 per 100 g.
- Shredded carrot (about 30%): 233 ml x 0.6 = 140 g. Carrot kcal ~41 per 100 g.
- Bell pepper strips, red and green (about 20%): 155 ml x 0.6 = 93 g. Bell pepper kcal ~31 per 100 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: the bottom of the bowl is partly obscured by the vegetable mound, but no separate base layer is evident, so no extra items are added.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (raw-prepared vegetables as served): onion 40, carrot 41, bell pepper 31.

Total weight ~466 g; energy ~ 233x0.40 + 140x0.41 + 93x0.31 = 93 + 57 + 29 = ~179 kcal.
